narration:
You are Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia,
and you’re the king of the AI gold rush.
Google, Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft, Elon Musk they’re all digging for gold.
But you’re the one selling the shovels.
Every company needs your chips.
Nvidia becomes the first company in history worth $5 trillion.
But you have no ego.
You wear the same leather jacket everywhere.
You even got the Nvidia logo tattooed on
your arm when your stock hit $100.
Most of your employees became millionaires.
People who used to fix graphics drivers are now driving Lambos to work.
Your company’s garage looks like a sports car showroom.
But your story didn’t start there.
As a teenager,
you used to wash dishes at Denny’s and clean a lot of toilets.
“I’ve cleaned more toilets than all of you combined.” Then one day,
you sit in a Denny’s booth with two friends and
start a company that makes chips for video games.
You call it Nvidia.
But within a few years, you almost go bankrupt.
Somehow, you survive.
Then, in 2006,
you put years of work and a lot of
money into making your gaming chips useful for science, not just games.
Everyone says you’re stupid.
And for years, nobody really uses it.
Then, in 2012,
a few researchers train an AI on two of your gaming cards,
and it destroys every other AI in a famous image contest.
Suddenly, the whole world wants your chips.
Now, every AI company on Earth is fighting to win the race.
But here’s the interesting part: it doesn’t matter who wins,
because whoever wins pays you.
Not bad for a dishwasher.
And if that wasn’t enough, your biggest rival in AI chips, AMD,
is run by Lisa Su, who happens to be your cousin.
The AI race is basically a family business.
But every king has a weakness.
America bans your best chips from China.
Yet reports say smugglers managed to sneak billions
of dollars’ worth of them in anyway.
Then,
The New York Times reports that US officials believe a top executive at Megape,
one of your biggest Asian customers, is a Chinese spy.
And that you had an affair with her.
You email your staff, apologising for being unfaithful to your wife.
Then comes a second affair, this time with one of your own vice presidents.
The FBI investigates your ties to the alleged spy.
Nvidia loses almost $200 billion in a single day.
And after 33 years, the king of the gold rush resigns.
You spent 33 years selling shovels to the whole world.
Turns out, you were digging your own grave.

Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-external-2026-11-15-1121.pdf

Jensen Huang helped turn NVIDIA from a struggling gaming-chip company into the engine behind the AI boom. This short follows his journey from washing dishes at Denny’s to leading one of the most valuable companies in the world.

But the story takes a dramatic turn as reported affairs, espionage allegations, China chip restrictions, and a sudden leadership crisis threaten to bring down the king of the AI gold rush.
